methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen that has raised $9.3M to date. The broader transportation sector includes six tracked private peers—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and EarthGrid—though no direct public comparables exist. A narrow peer-median approach is not applicable here; the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with comparable valuation tiers to support a reliable multiples-based triangulation.

The stage-progression method is the primary valuation lever available. Using the $9.3M in total capital raised as a proxy for entry valuation, a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier applied to seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $23.25M. This method assumes Infinite Machine's risk and growth profile align with historical seed-stage venture outcomes in the transportation sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $27M (high), with a median of $23M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty around product-market fit validation, capital efficiency, and the company's ability to execute toward Series A milestones. The narrow peer set and absence of public market reference points further limit confidence in any point estimate. Refinement would benefit from tracking additional early-stage transportation company outcomes or obtaining more granular financial metrics from Infinite Machine itself.
